name: Growth OS — 2. Send the next sequence step

nodes.name: 10:00 and 13:00 Dhaka, Sun-Thu
nodes.notes: Two passes a day inside Bangladeshi working hours. Never Friday or Saturday.

parameters.query:
-- Everything the sender needs, resolved in ONE query: the enrollment, the prospect,
-- and the NEXT step's template. A reply, a bounce or a manual opt-out has already
-- flipped the enrollment out of 'active' (DB trigger), so no extra guard is needed here.
select e.id            as enrollment_id,
       e.current_step,
       p.id             as prospect_id,
       p.hotel_name,
       p.city,
       p.rooms,
       p.email,
       p.owner_name,
       p.manager_name,
       s.subject        as subject_template,
       s.body_template,
       s.step_number
  from public.sequence_enrollments e
  join public.prospects     p on p.id = e.prospect_id
  join public.sequences    sq on sq.id = e.sequence_id and sq.is_active
  join public.sequence_steps s on s.sequence_id = e.sequence_id
                              and s.step_number  = e.current_step + 1
 where e.status = 'active'
   and e.next_send_at <= now()
   and p.do_not_contact = false
   and p.email is not null
 order by p.score desc
 limit 40;

nodes.name: One at a time
nodes.notes: Sequential sends keep the per-second rate low and make a mid-run failure recoverable — anything already sent is already logged.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ from: 'Shan <shan@go.fountainbd.com>', reply_to: 'shanwazahmed@fountainbd.com', to: [$json.email], subject: $json.subject, text: $json.body, headers: { 'List-Unsubscribe': '<mailto:shanwazahmed@fountainbd.com?subject=unsubscribe>' } }) }}

nodes.name: Send via Resend
nodes.notes: PLAIN TEXT only (`text`, not `html`). No tracking pixel, no image, one link at most. From MUST be the go. subdomain — never the root domain that carries the hotel's booking mail.

parameters.query:
-- One transaction per successful send: log the touch (the trigger stamps the
-- prospect's status and last_contact_at), record the provider message id, and
-- advance the enrollment to the next step at that step's delay.
with logged as (
  insert into public.activities (prospect_id, type, direction, outcome, subject, body, created_by)
  values ($1::uuid, 'email', 'outbound', 'sent', $2, $3, 'n8n')
  returning prospect_id
),
evt as (
  insert into public.email_events (prospect_id, message_id, provider, event, payload)
  values ($1::uuid, $4, 'resend', 'sent', jsonb_build_object('step', $5::int))
  returning id
),
nxt as (
  select coalesce(min(s.delay_days), null) as delay_days
    from public.sequence_steps s
    join public.sequence_enrollments e on e.sequence_id = s.sequence_id
   where e.id = $6::uuid and s.step_number = $5::int + 1
)
update public.sequence_enrollments e
   set current_step = $5::int,
       next_send_at = case when nxt.delay_days is null then null
                           else now() + (nxt.delay_days || ' days')::interval end,
       status       = case when nxt.delay_days is null then 'completed' else 'active' end
  from nxt
 where e.id = $6::uuid;

parameters.query:
-- A failed send is NOT silently retried forever. Pause the enrollment and record
-- why, so a broken address or a provider block shows up in the pipeline instead of
-- quietly burning sending reputation.
update public.sequence_enrollments
   set status = 'paused', stopped_reason = left($2, 300), next_send_at = null
 where id = $1::uuid;

meta.description: Sends the next due step of the cold email sequence, one prospect at a time, and advances the enrollment. Replies stop the sequence via a database trigger, not here.
